correctness.rationale: Every actual majority flip strictly reduces the number of disagreeing edges, and only all-zero and all-one fixed points exist, proving a.s. absorption. With both hubs one, if j>=floor(s/2) they are stable; otherwise the competition among s-j eligible zero-leaves and the two unstable hubs has successive probabilities (s-j-i)/(s-j-i+2), giving the telescoping Φ_s(j). With opposed hubs, leaves remain tied and the first effective hub flip determines consensus by whether 2j<s,=s,>s; when equality both hub clocks are equally likely. Complementation handles zero hubs. The K_2,s threshold is ceil(s/2), so odd s changes the exact product by (s+3)/((s+1)(s+2)), even s zero. Independently solved exact rational count-state recurrences for 176 macrostates at small s, matching all kernel cases. This finite check supports but is not the all-s proof.
